verses.en: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
verses.pt: Sabes tu o tempo do parto das cabras montesas, ou podes observar quando é que parem as corças?
verses.en_web: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
verses.en_bbe: Have you knowledge of the rock-goats? or do you see the roes giving birth to their young?

verses.en: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
verses.pt: Podes contar os meses que cumprem, ou sabes o tempo do seu parto?
verses.en_web: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
verses.en_bbe: Is the number of their months fixed by you? or is the time when they give birth ordered by you?

verses.en: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.
verses.pt: Encurvam-se, dão à luz as suas crias, lançam de si a sua prole.
verses.en_web: They bow themselves, they bear their young. They end their labor pains.
verses.en_bbe: They are bent down, they give birth to their young, they let loose the fruit of their body.

verses.en: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.
verses.pt: Seus filhos enrijam, crescem no campo livre; saem, e não tornam para elas:
verses.en_web: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
verses.en_bbe: Their young ones are strong, living in the open country; they go out and do not come back again.

verses.en: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
verses.pt: Quem despediu livre o jumento montês, e quem soltou as prisões ao asno veloz,
verses.en_web: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
verses.en_bbe: Who has let the ass of the fields go free? or made loose the bands of the loud-voiced beast?

verses.en: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.
verses.pt: ao qual dei o ermo por casa, e a terra salgada por morada?
verses.en_web: Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
verses.en_bbe: To whom I have given the waste land for a heritage, and the salt land as a living-place.

verses.en: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.
verses.pt: Ele despreza o tumulto da cidade; não obedece os gritos do condutor.
verses.en_web: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
verses.en_bbe: He makes sport of the noise of the town; the voice of the driver does not come to his ears;

verses.en: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
verses.pt: O circuito das montanhas é o seu pasto, e anda buscando tudo o que está verde.
verses.en_web: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.
verses.en_bbe: He goes looking for his grass-lands in the mountains, searching out every green thing.

verses.en: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?
verses.pt: Quererá o boi selvagem servir-te? ou ficará junto à tua manjedoura?
verses.en_web: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
verses.en_bbe: Will the ox of the mountains be your servant? or is his night's resting-place by your food-store?

verses.en: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
verses.pt: Podes amarrar o boi selvagem ao arado com uma corda, ou esterroará ele após ti os vales?
verses.en_web: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
verses.en_bbe: Will he be pulling your plough with cords, turning up the valleys after you?

verses.en: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?
verses.pt: Ou confiarás nele, por ser grande a sua força, ou deixarás a seu cargo o teu trabalho?
verses.en_web: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
verses.en_bbe: Will you put your faith in him, because his strength is great? will you give the fruit of your work into his care?

verses.en: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?
verses.pt: Fiarás dele que te torne o que semeaste e o recolha à tua eira?
verses.en_web: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
verses.en_bbe: Will you be looking for him to come back, and get in your seed to the crushing-floor?

verses.en: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?
verses.pt: Movem-se alegremente as asas da avestruz; mas é benigno o adorno da sua plumagem?
verses.en_web: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
verses.en_bbe: Is the wing of the ostrich feeble, or is it because she has no feathers,

verses.en: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,
verses.pt: Pois ela deixa os seus ovos na terra, e os aquenta no pó,
verses.en_web: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
verses.en_bbe: That she puts her eggs on the earth, warming them in the dust,

verses.en: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.
verses.pt: e se esquece de que algum pé os pode pisar, ou de que a fera os pode calcar.
verses.en_web: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
verses.en_bbe: Without a thought that they may be crushed by the foot, and broken by the beasts of the field?

verses.en: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;
verses.pt: Endurece-se para com seus filhos, como se não fossem seus; embora se perca o seu trabalho, ela está sem temor;
verses.en_web: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
verses.en_bbe: She is cruel to her young ones, as if they were not hers; her work is to no purpose; she has no fear.

verses.en: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.
verses.pt: porque Deus a privou de sabedoria, e não lhe repartiu entendimento.
verses.en_web: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
verses.en_bbe: For God has taken wisdom from her mind, and given her no measure of knowledge.

verses.en: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.
verses.pt: Quando ela se levanta para correr, zomba do cavalo, e do cavaleiro.
verses.en_web: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
verses.en_bbe: When she is shaking her wings on high, she makes sport of the horse and of him who is seated on him.

verses.en: Hath thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?
verses.pt: Acaso deste força ao cavalo, ou revestiste de força o seu pescoço?
verses.en_web: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
verses.en_bbe: Do you give strength to the horse? is it by your hand that his neck is clothed with power?

verses.en: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.
verses.pt: Fizeste-o pular como o gafanhoto? Terrível é o fogoso respirar das suas ventas.
verses.en_web: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
verses.en_bbe: Is it through you that he is shaking like a locust, in the pride of his loud-sounding breath?

verses.en: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.
verses.pt: Escarva no vale, e folga na sua força, e sai ao encontro dos armados.
verses.en_web: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
verses.en_bbe: He is stamping with joy in the valley; he makes sport of fear.

verses.en: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.
verses.pt: Ri-se do temor, e não se espanta; e não torna atrás por causa da espada.
verses.en_web: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
verses.en_bbe: In his strength he goes out against the arms of war, turning not away from the sword.

verses.en: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.
verses.pt: Sobre ele rangem a aljava, a lança cintilante e o dardo.
verses.en_web: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
verses.en_bbe: The bow is sounding against him; he sees the shining point of spear and arrow.

verses.en: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.
verses.pt: Tremendo e enfurecido devora a terra, e não se contém ao som da trombeta.
verses.en_web: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
verses.en_bbe: Shaking with passion, he is biting the earth; he is not able to keep quiet at the sound of the horn;

verses.en: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
verses.pt: Toda vez que soa a trombeta, diz: Eia! E de longe cheira a guerra, e o trovão dos capitães e os gritos.
verses.en_web: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
verses.en_bbe: When it comes to his ears he says, Aha! He is smelling the fight from far off, and hearing the thunder of the captains, and the war-cries.

verses.en: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?
verses.pt: É pelo teu entendimento que se eleva o gavião, e estende as suas asas para o sul?
verses.en_web: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
verses.en_bbe: Is it through your knowledge that the hawk takes his flight, stretching out his wings to the south?

verses.en: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?
verses.pt: Ou se remonta a águia ao teu mandado, e põe no alto o seu ninho?
verses.en_web: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
verses.en_bbe: Or is it by your orders that the eagle goes up, and makes his resting-place on high?

verses.en: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.
verses.pt: Mora nas penhas e ali tem a sua pousada, no cume das penhas, no lugar seguro.
verses.en_web: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
verses.en_bbe: On the rock is his house, and on the mountain-top his strong place.

verses.en: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.
verses.pt: Dali descobre a presa; seus olhos a avistam de longe.
verses.en_web: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
verses.en_bbe: From there he is watching for food; his eye sees it far off.

verses.en: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.
verses.pt: Seus filhos chupam o sangue; e onde há mortos, ela aí está.
verses.en_web: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
verses.en_bbe: His young have blood for their drink, and where the dead bodies are, there is he to be seen.
